title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, and Comms (2026 Update)
author: Aisha Rao
summary: Canonical company playbook for on-call operations and incident response at Redwood Inference. Covers incident lifecycle, severity definitions, runbook catalog and examples, rotation & escalation policies, game day guidance, postmortem templates and timelines, and status page / customer communications templates.
body:
Purpose
This document defines Redwood Inference's standard process for detecting, triaging, mitigating, and learning from incidents that impact availability, latency, correctness, or data security for customer-facing inference services (hosted API, Dedicated, Private). It is the canonical reference for on-call engineers, incident commanders (ICs), and stakeholders.

Scope
- Services: Redwood API (hosted inference), Dedicated control plane, Private deployments control plane, router/smart-routing, KV/prefix cache, and telemetry pipelines that affect customer-visible SLOs.
- Activities: Alerting & paging, incident lifecycle, runbooks and operational playbooks, rotations & escalation, game days & readiness exercises, postmortems and RCA, and customer/status communications.

1) Incident severity and definitions
We use a four-tier severity model. The definition focuses on customer impact and required response time.
- Sev0 (Critical, "SEV0"): Major outage or data-loss affecting >10% of active customers or preventing the product from functioning for most users. Requires immediate pager, IC within 15 minutes.
- Sev1 (High): Significant degradation in latency/throughput or partial outage impacting a subset of customers (>=1 high-value customer or multiple internal routes). IC within 30 minutes.
- Sev2 (Medium): Degraded performance that impacts non-critical functionality or small groups of users. Response within 4 business hours.
- Sev3 (Low): Informational incidents, alerts that don’t require immediate action. Monitored/triaged as part of backlog.

Key SLO thresholds (examples)
- Hosted API availability SLO: 99.95% monthly.
- Median request latency (GPU inference): <120ms for 512-token gen under standard plan.
- Error rate alert threshold: >0.3% for 5m sustained or a 5x increase over baseline.

2) Roles & responsibilities
- Pager/Primary on-call (Responder): First to receive alert, performs initial triage and follows runbooks.
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates response, declares severity, owns communications (internal + status page), and authorizes escalations and mitigations.
- Subject Matter Expert (SME): Service owners for runtime, routing, infra, or networking who provide deep technical analysis.
- Communications Lead: Owns customer & internal comms templates, updates status page, and notifies Sales/CS as needed.
- Postmortem Author: Usually the IC or primary SME tasked with drafting the RCA and remediation plan.

3) Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)
Detection -> Triage -> Mitigation -> Restore -> Post-incident analysis
- Detection: Alerts are generated by monitoring (Prometheus + Alertmanager and cloud metrics) or customer reports (support, status page). PagerDuty (or equivalent) is the single source of truth for paging.
- Triage (first 10 minutes): Responder acknowledges alert, validates impact (scope, customers affected, SLOs), and attempts quick mitigations per runbook. If impact meets Sev1/Sev0, escalate to IC.
- Declare: IC formally declares incident severity, creates an incident channel (Slack #incident-<YYYYMMDD>-<service>) and incident doc (Confluence or incident tracker entry).
- Mitigation: Follow runbooks for targeted mitigation. Prioritize actions that minimize customer impact even if temporary (roll back, traffic shift, scale up, degrade non-essential features).
- Restore: Confirm service is restored to healthy state and SLOs are within normal bounds for at least 30 minutes.
- Postmortem: IC or Postmortem Author starts the RCA within 48 hours; a complete postmortem (with remediation and owners) is required within 10 business days for Sev1/Sev0.

4) Escalation policy & communication cadence
- Pager escalation: If primary does not acknowledge within 5 minutes for SEV0 or 15 minutes for SEV1, Alertmanager escalates to on-call lead, then to the SRE manager.
- IC cadence: 15-minute check-ins for SEV0 until stable, 30-minute for SEV1.
- Internal stakeholder updates: Brief summary every 30 minutes for SEV0 (first 2 hours), then hourly.

5) Runbook catalog & example runbooks
We maintain a live index of runbooks in Confluence. Each runbook includes purpose, preconditions, verification steps, rollback steps, and common diagnostic commands. Examples below.

Runbook: High 5xx Error Rate on Hosting API
- Symptoms: >0.3% 5xx over 5m, rising request queue on inference frontend, increased retries in router logs.
- Preconditions: Access to service logs, Grafana dashboards: api-errors, request-queue, model-kv-hit-rate.
- Quick mitigation steps (ordered):
  1) Confirm scope: query last 15 minutes by region/route.
  2) If a specific route/model is affected, remove route from traffic using router service: curl -X POST $ROUTER/admin/drain-route -d '{"route":"<route>"}'
  3) If backend GPU node(s) show OOMs, cordon nodes and scale up GPU pool: terraformscale gpool --add 2 --region $REGION
  4) If third-party dependency (auth/db) causing 5xx, failover DB read-replicas or revert recent schema deploy.
- Verification: 5xx rate back to <0.1% sustained for 15 minutes, no customer reports.
- Post-incident remediation: Create task to fix root cause (bug, capacity, or config) and assign owner.

Runbook: Latency spike due to KV cache miss storm
- Symptoms: Median token latency increases, KV cache miss rate > 60% and sustained.
- Quick mitigations:
  1) Enable degraded mode: disable prefetching for non-critical routes.
  2) Roll traffic to warmed model variant (quantized / cached snapshot).
  3) If cache service is unhealthy, restart cache cluster per restart playbook: kubectl -n infra scale statefulset/cache --replicas=0 && sleep 30 && kubectl scale --replicas=3
- Verification: Median latency returns to baseline across sample requests (15m).

Runbook: Private deployment control plane unreachable (customer on-prem)
- Steps:
  1) Confirm network path: traceroute and curl to control plane endpoints.
  2) Validate customer-provided firewall rules and VPN health.
  3) Offer temporary local fallback (standalone agent) and coordinate with Private Deployments team.

6) On-call rotations and coverage
- Primary rotation: 1-week handoff windows (Mon 09:00 PT -> next Mon 09:00 PT).
- Secondary/backup on-call: rotates monthly and is paged for SEV1+ when primary cannot respond.
- Purple team (weekend): rotating 2-person coverage for weekends; primary is paid on-call and compensated per policy in company handbook.
- Handoffs: Outgoing on-call must publish a Handoff note in Slack #oncall-handoffs with known issues, ongoing mitigations, and outstanding alerts. Handoffs must include: active incidents, follow-ups, and runbook changes.
- Scheduling: Schedules are published in PagerDuty and the team calendar. Escalation contacts and phone numbers must be kept up-to-date in the oncall roster doc.

7) Game days & readiness exercises
Purpose: Validate runbooks, paging, cross-team coordination, and the recovery path for major failure modes.
- Frequency: Minimum one exercise per quarter, at least one cross-functional (runtime, infra, support, product) game day per year.
- Scenarios to test: GPU-fleet partial outage, global router partition, KV cache cold-start, control plane HA failover, incident caused by a bad rollout.
- Post-game-day deliverables: Action items, runbook updates, and an executive summary with measured MTTR and lessons learned.

8) Postmortem process & template
Requirements:
- For SEV1/SEV0: Draft postmortem within 48 hours, final within 10 business days.
- Include timeline, root cause, remediation (short/long-term), and measurable success criteria for fixes.
- Postmortems are blameless; focus on process and system improvements.

Postmortem template (fields to include)
- Title
- Incident ID / PagerDuty link
- Severity and impact summary (customers affected, duration, SLOs impacted)
- Timeline (UTC) with notable events and owner initials
- Root cause analysis (why did this happen?)
- Contributing factors (alerts, testing gaps, rollout issues)
- Mitigation & recovery steps taken
- Action items (owner, due date, verification criteria)
- Postmortem reviewer(s) and sign-off
- Public customer summary (short version for status page / CS)

9) Status page & customer communications templates
We operate a public status.redwood.ai page and an internal private incident page for customers with dedicated contact channels (for Dedicated/Private customers). Use these templates and get Communications Lead sign-off before public posts for SEV1/SEV0.

Status page template (brief)
- Title: Partial outage affecting Hosted API (region: us-west-2)
- Status: Identified / Investigating / Monitoring / Resolved
- Impact: Customers in us-west-2 may experience increased latency or 5xx errors for text generation routes.
- Latest update: [Timestamp UTC] We have identified a routing misconfiguration and are routing traffic away from the affected pool. Mitigation in progress.
- Next update: [ETA or timeframe]

Customer notification email template (for CS / Sales use)
Subject: Service impact update – Redwood Inference hosted API (us-west-2)
Hi <Customer Name>,
We are investigating an issue affecting the Redwood hosted API in us-west-2 which may cause increased latency and intermittent errors. Our engineers have identified the likely cause and put a mitigation in place to route traffic away from affected capacity. We will share a follow-up once service is restored.
If you have urgent concerns or are experiencing data loss, please reply to this message and we will prioritize.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Incident Response Team

10) Post-incident metrics & verification
- Verification checkpoints: post-mitigation check at 30 minutes, final verification at 24 hours.
- Required metrics to confirm closure: sustained SLO compliance for 24 hours, incident alert noise reduced, and no related alerts for the same root cause in 7 days.

11) Runbook lifecycle and ownership
- Every runbook must list an owner and last-reviewed date. Owners must review runbooks quarterly or after any related incident.
- Runbook changes require PRs in the runbook repo and a 1-week review window for substantive changes.

12) Tools & observability references (quick links)
- PagerDuty: oncall schedule & pager history
- Grafana: dashboards -> API / Router / KV / GPU-Fleet
- Kibana: logs -> infer-front, router, backend-models
- Confluence runbook index: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-index
- Status page editor: status.redwood.ai/admin

13) Appendix: Example checklists for IC
Initial 15-minute checklist (IC)
1) Confirm primary responder and acknowledge.
2) Create incident channel and incident doc.
3) Classify severity and notify stakeholders.
4) Identify immediate mitigations from runbook.
5) Track actions in incident doc and assign owners.

IC wrap-up checklist
1) Confirm restoration and SLO verification.
2) Draft postmortem timeline and assign postmortem owner.
3) Publish initial customer-facing summary.
4) Close incident in PagerDuty and update status page to Resolved when appropriate.

Ownership & maintenance
Document owner: SRE Team (oncall rotation lead)
Next review date: 2026-05-01

Feedback and change process
Submit updates as PRs to the runbooks repo or request edits via the #oncall-docs Slack channel. Major process changes require SRE and Product sign-off.

End of document
